Some changes needed to handling (not very many, just minor adjustments). New career mode is awesome and immersive. Really wish EA wasn't so greedy with the content that's included in the game this time around...one helmet, fire suit and gloves and everything else needs to be purchased? That's a bit of greed if I've ever seen it. Overall, great offering this year. I'm sure the usual detractors will still...detract. 

Hardly any DNF's for AI drivers, no crashes for AI drivers through 8 races at 50%, unable to equip wet or intermediate tires if the grand prix starts with rain coming down, especially in F2 races and the AI seems to be just as fast on slicks in the wet as you are on wet weather tires. Hopefully, the patch that's coming out won't screw up other things like it has in the past 2-3 games. 

Other than this, I'm thoroughly enjoying racing in my single player career. I enjoy the new rivalry systems. Makes for much more interesting races having to potentially out race 3 drivers (including your teammate now) in addition to trying to finish well.

Just have some fun with the GAME everyone. There are no F1 contracts waiting for any of us. ;)

Career Experience: The game has a career mode like most of the other F1 games, simply go in and race your calendar, not much more to it. Buy this game if that's what you are looking for.

Physics: God aweful physics. Other F1 games at least make an attempt to deliver a life like braking experience. However, if you want to be fast in this game you have to lock your brakes into every corner which ruins the whole experience of F1. In real life locking up would have you lose tenths but here you gain them. For such a long standing franchise representing a high caliber motorsport, it's mind boggling how realistic physics are still unachievable 3 years after a regulation change. 

Multiplayer: Non existent garbage, don't bother. You'll just spend most of it waiting in a queue just to race 3 dimwits.

Review:
For €10, I find the game to be quite enjoyable, leaning more towards an arcade style than a simcade experience. The cars feel overly responsive, with a noticeable amount of rear grip that makes it difficult to lose control unless you're really pushing the limits. In terms of visuals, with RTGI enabled, the game looks better than F1 23, but that's where the comparison ends.
The sound design is still lacking, with the exception of the replay sounds, which are more polished. As for the physics, while there have been improvements since launch, they still fall short when compared to F1 23.

If you can catch the game on sale (which is a last chance, by the way), it’s worth picking up. At full price, however, I would recommend waiting for the next installment in 2025.

Initial Thoughts:
Despite the recent post-launch patch, the game's physics remain underwhelming. In comparison, the 2023 physics were far more refined, but EA and Codemasters seem to have taken a step backward in this area.

tldr.text: Mostly Positive (71%): players praise the graphics and art, and recent reviews are noticeably more positive than the all-time score.
The main complaint, raised in 18% of reviews, is bugs and crashes.

details.text: Players with under 2 hours logged are far less positive than longer-time players, and the mood shifts once they pass two hours.
Buyers should know that 6% of reviews complain about developers and updates, and one reviewer says the game is "getting worse with every update".
